{{short description|Belgian mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2021}}
'''Lucien Godeaux''' (1887–1975) was a prolific [[Belgians|Belgian]] mathematician. His total of more than 1000 papers and books, 644 of which are found in [[Mathematical Reviews]], made him one of the most published mathematicians.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Grossman |first=Jerrold W. |title=Patterns of Research in Mathematics |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=52 |issue=1 |pages=35–41 |date=January 2005 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200501/200501-body-pdf.html |access-date=2025-08-29}}</ref> He was the sole author of all but one of his papers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.santafe.edu/~mark/papers/cnlspre.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=9 August 2007 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070809084805/http://www.santafe.edu/~mark/papers/cnlspre.pdf |archivedate=9 August 2007 |df=dmy-all }}.</ref>

He is best remembered for work in [[algebraic geometry]]. From [[Liège]], he was attracted to the work of the [[Italian school of algebraic geometry]] by the work of one of its masters, [[Federigo Enriques]]. Godeaux went to [[Bologna]] to study with him. The [[Godeaux surface]] is a construction of a special type, which has subsequently been much studied.

Since 2007, the Belgian Mathematical Society (BMS) is organising a "Godeaux lecture" in his memory.
